items.work: J. van Vloten and J. P. N. Land, eds., Benedicti de Spinoza Opera quotquot reperta sunt, Volumen prius (Hagae Comitum: apud Martinum Nijhoff, MDCCCLXXXII [1882]) — the Tractatus de intellectus emendatione, the Ethica ordine geometrico demonstrata, the Tractatus politicus and the Tractatus theologico-politicus in Latin, in the critical edition; University of Toronto copy

scope: The first volume of van Vloten and Land's Opera quotquot reperta sunt (1882), in Latin: the Tractatus de intellectus emendatione, the Ethica, the Tractatus politicus and the Tractatus theologico-politicus. QUEUED: the first editions, the Tractatus theologico-politicus of 1670 (the open scans found carry ProQuest's copyright notice on every image, so their licence cannot be verified at the file) and the Opera posthuma of 1677 (the one open copy found is a truncated PDF without its trailer, which no reader opens); the second volume of van Vloten and Land, with the Epistolae and the Principia philosophiae Cartesianae; the Korte Verhandeling in Dutch.

why_seated: MANUS, 27 October 2026, after the twenty-sixth seating: "deleuze and guattari... no way around that copyright, huh?" Told that every route through it is closed for decades, and offered a declared absence for them and the open sources they read: "yes - i cant believe we havent seated spinoza yet. yes to all" — and "and leibniz' monodology only". Spinoza is seated as the first of the sources Deleuze read: Spinoza et le problème de l'expression (1968), Spinoza: philosophie pratique (1970; 1981), and the substance, expression and conatus of the Ethica through Mille plateaux.
ruling: Seated in the language each wrote in, as far as the public domain of the United States reaches and an open witness was found, beside the declared absence of Deleuze and Guattari (27/07) (MANUS, 2026-10-27).
